minutes.headline: District previews FY27-29 outlook, asking to restore staff cut in FY26; no vote was taken.
minutes.summary: The select board, finance committee and school committee met jointly to hear a preliminary, forward-looking FY27-29 school budget outlook, explicitly deferring any FY25 questions to a later public forum. The superintendent and business manager walked through contractual assumptions (salaries, health insurance, utilities, transportation) and a series of requested staff restorations -- interventionists, a kindergarten paraprofessional, a world-language teacher, a music teacher, a bridge/TLC program, an ELL teacher, and a debated full-time athletic director/assistant principal split -- framed as restoring FY26 cuts rather than new expansion. No formal votes were taken on any budget item; the boards adjourned after discussion, with several follow-up items assigned to the administration for the next budget cycle.

votes.motion: Adjourn the select board at 9:52 p.m.

budget_items.what_was_said: The district assumed a 20% annual health insurance increase for FY27 through FY29, projecting a large rise from FY23 actuals.
Electricity costs were shown rising from FY23 to a much higher FY29 projection, tied to a locked-in per-kWh rate with the district's provider.
Heating costs were projected lower than electricity and are currently under review for possible savings.
The transportation contract is described as effectively uncompetitive since no other vendor has bid in years, making the cost locked in regardless of market forces.
The general education transportation line was under-budgeted for FY26 despite being under contract, which will require a line-item transfer.
A requested 1.0 interventionist position to address early literacy and math gaps, costed at a master's-with-experience salary step.
A new kindergarten paraprofessional position was proposed, to be funded by the primary school through reductions in general supplies.
A board member asked what the paraprofessional salary works out to hourly, comparing it unfavorably to retail wages.
A new world language teacher is requested to avoid delaying language instruction or cutting the Latin program for a large incoming class.
The Turkey Hill interventionist restoration carries an associated insurance cost figure discussed alongside the high school positions.
Of the two new high school positions, only one carries a health insurance cost since the other is already part-time with insurance.
Adding one van with a monitor to a transportation route that can't be regionalized for two students was cited as a striking cost example.
A guesstimated salary range was given for making the athletic director position full-time again.
The athletic director was previously paid as a stipend rather than a full position, cited to contrast with the current full-time ask.

Eliminating the reading coach and converting the math coach to a partly direct-service instructional specialist role was costed as a small net add, since the individual would move to the teachers' contract.

budget_items.topic: Data reporting manager / assistant business manager restructuring
budget_items.what_was_said: Reducing the data reporting manager to half-time while adding a new assistant business manager position was presented as a net savings.
The net effect of the central office restructuring was summarized as roughly breakeven once insurance costs were included.
The estimated total cost of all proposed restorations and restructuring, assuming highest-tier insurance for all new hires, was presented as the headline ask.
The remaining available FY25 budget and percent used were reported as the year wrapped up.

budget_items.topic: FY26 total budget with free cash
budget_items.what_was_said: The FY26 total budget including one-time free cash was broken into salaries and expenses.
Level-service FY27 salaries and expenses were projected without any of the new requested positions included.
FY28 projections show expenses rising notably, driven largely by health insurance and special education cost growth.
FY29 projections were given as the final year of the three-year outlook.
Excluding the one-time free cash, the level-service FY27 budget represents a percentage increase over FY26.

budget_items.topic: FY26 free cash split between salaries and expenses
budget_items.what_was_said: Of the $500,000 in free cash used in FY26, most but not all was applied to salaries.
Combining the level-service budget with the cost of restored positions produced the total needs-based FY27 figure.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance estimate vs. actual (override context)
budget_items.what_was_said: During the override discussion, the health insurance increase was initially estimated much higher than what it actually came in at, prompting a request to isolate that line going forward.
A count of district staff currently enrolled in some form of health insurance was given as roughly half to sixty percent of staff.

budget_items.topic: Cherry sheet school choice tuition-in revenue decline
budget_items.what_was_said: Incoming school-choice tuition revenue on the cherry sheet has fallen sharply over five to six years, shifting cost onto the town budget.

budget_items.topic: School choice per-pupil funding vs. cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The district receives a set amount per accepted school-choice student but the district's own per-pupil cost is much higher.
Spending on social workers and guidance rose sharply from FY24 to FY25, prompting a question about whether the level can be reduced.
Psychologist services spending also rose from FY24 to FY25.
A running total of fee revenue collected this year from bus and athletic fees was reported as higher than expected.

budget_items.topic: Student Opportunity Act funding to neighboring districts
budget_items.what_was_said: A state senator's forum remark that Leominster and Fitchburg have received substantially more Student Opportunity Act funding was cited as context for state funding disparities.

decisions.decision: Business manager to research and report back on the source of negative transfers shown in the FY25 budget summary.
Presenters agreed to isolate and separately report the health insurance cost increase from the total budget ask going forward, so the override/budget conversation doesn't repeat prior confusion.
Business office to provide a roster-level breakdown of health plan enrollment (family vs. individual, by count) to support more precise budgeting of new positions' insurance costs.
Superintendent to provide historical math/reading achievement data over time to the requesting board member.
Administration to bring back more history on when the athletic director position moved from part-time to full-time, and a data-backed model for any renewed AD proposal.
Administration agreed to present a plan/budget picture for grants and revolving funds, with and without grant funding, as part of the next budget cycle.

A board member is drafting a proposed regulatory/statutory revision to shift medically-related out-of-district service costs onto private insurance, continuing prior advocacy on bus-contract competitive bidding requirements.

what_happened.line: Three boards jointly previewed a forward-looking FY27-29 school budget outlook; no votes were taken on any item.

The district asked to restore several staff positions cut in FY26 -- interventionists, a kindergarten paraprofessional, world language and music teachers, an ELL teacher -- framed as restoration rather than expansion.
A full-time athletic director/assistant principal restoration was debated without resolution; administration was asked to bring back position history and a data-backed model.
The business manager will research the source of negative transfers shown in the FY25 budget summary, with FY25 questions otherwise deferred to a later public forum.
Presenters agreed to report health insurance cost increases separately from the total budget ask, and to provide roster-level health plan enrollment detail for the next budget cycle.

why_it_matters: These are preview requests for the FY27 budget residents will eventually vote on at town meeting; nothing here is a commitment or a final figure.

Health insurance and utility cost assumptions shown in this preview flow into the same budget-versus-override conversation that has confused residents in past cycles, which is why presenters agreed to break the insurance line out separately.

Whether the district can distinguish grant-funded and general-fund positions -- requested for the next cycle -- affects how residents should read any staffing line as a town cost versus a grant that could end.
watch_next: The later public forum where deferred FY25 questions, including the negative-transfer explanation, will be addressed.
Next budget cycle's presentation, expected to include a grants/revolving-fund breakdown and roster-level health insurance detail.
